headline: Water is the only substance that exists naturally in all three states
universal_truth: Like water, we too can transform while remaining ourselves
fun_facts: The same water that dinosaurs drank 65 million years ago is still cycling through Earth today
Hot water can freeze faster than cold water—a phenomenon called the Mpemba effect that still puzzles scientists
There's enough water in Earth's mantle to fill the oceans three times over
discussion_questions: How have you transformed while staying fundamentally yourself?
What conditions help you flow versus freeze?
Where in your life could you be more adaptable?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Look at a glass of water. Simple, right? But that water has lived more lives than you can imagine. It's been ice, steam, cloud, river, and ocean—possibly for billions of years. Today, we explore what water's transformations teach us.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Here's something strange: the water you drink today might have passed through a dinosaur. Water doesn't get created or destroyed—it just keeps transforming. What makes these transformations possible?
cliff.prompt: What causes water to change states?

options.response: Exactly. Temperature changes cause molecules to speed up or slow down.
That can affect it, but the primary driver is simpler...

q1.title: Ancient Water
q1.script: Every drop of water on Earth has been here for about 4.5 billion years. The water in your morning coffee might have been part of an ancient glacier, a medieval rain shower, or yes—passed through a dinosaur. Water molecules are nearly indestructible.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Ancient Water"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Mpemba Effect
q2.script: Here's a mystery: under certain conditions, hot water freezes faster than cold water. Named after a Tanzanian student who noticed it in the 1960s, the Mpemba effect still isn't fully explained. Even water keeps secrets.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Hidden Oceans
q3.script: Scientists discovered there's three times more water locked in minerals deep in Earth's mantle than in all our surface oceans combined. Water is everywhere—even where we can't see it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Water teaches us that transformation doesn't mean losing yourself. Ice, liquid, and steam are all still H2O. You can change forms—careers, beliefs, relationships—while staying fundamentally you.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 2. Tomorrow, we'll look up and discover where clouds come from. Until then, notice the water around you—and remember its billion-year journey.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Adaptability - Flowing Like Water
growTrack.learning_objective: Practice adapting to change with grace
growTrack.activity: Think of one situation where you're resisting change. Ask yourself: 'What would water do?' Write down one way you could flow around this obstacle instead of pushing against it.
